name: Simmered Frozen Tofu Soup With Pork and Cabbage

ingredients.name: Napa cabbage, from about half a 2 3/4-pound head

instructions.primary_message: Drain the firm tofu of packing liquid. Peel and thinly slice the fresh ginger. Smash the garlic. Very thinly slice the boneless skinless pork belly.
instructions.secondary_message:
0.45 kg firm tofu
1 (4 cm) knob fresh ginger
4 medium cloves garlic
155 g boneless skinless pork belly

instructions.primary_message: Place tofu in a sealed container or on a tray wrapped with plastic and freeze for at least 3 hours and up to 6 months. When fully frozen, the tofu will turn a darker shade of yellow/brown and become slightly translucent.

When ready to cook, fully thaw the tofu, at least 3 hours at room temperature or 8 hours in the fridge. Gently squeeze the tofu between your palms to express as much water as possible without damaging it. Cut tofu into 10 equally sized pieces.

Core the Napa cabbage and separate the leaves. Cut the tender portions from the thicker stem of each Napa cabbage leaf. Tear tender portions into roughly 5-cm pieces, and cut thick stems into roughly 13-cm by 2.5-cm strips. Keep separate and set aside.

In a large Dutch oven, heat oil over medium-high heat until lightly smoking. Add ginger and sauté until lightly browned around edges, about 30 seconds. Add garlic and cook until lightly browned, about 15 seconds. Add sliced pork and cook, stirring, until last traces of pink are gone, about 30 seconds.

Add sliced Napa cabbage stems and cook, stirring, until they begin to soften, about 30 seconds. Stir in soy sauce and cook until mostly dry, about 30 seconds. Add the torn cabbage leaves, followed by the chicken stock and water. Bring to a boil.
Add the tofu to the pot along with the salt and chicken bouillon. Return to a boil, cover, and let simmer until the Napa cabbage stems have softened, about 5 minutes.

Season with salt, if necessary. Add soaked rice noodles, and let simmer until the rice noodles are soft and cooked through, about 2 minutes (note that cooking time will depend on the type of rice noodle you use). Serve warm with white rice.

schema_metadata.keywords: frozen and thawed tofu soup, frozen simmered tofu, tofu, pork, and cabbage soup, frozen simmered tofu soup with pork and cabbage, rice vermicelli, tofu and pork soup, tofu and cabbage soup

description: Freezing and thawing tofu transforms its texture, making it the perfect vehicle for flavor.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 6 hr 25 min.

Optional or for serving: Cooked long-grain white rice, for serving

Optional substitutions: very thinly sliced boneless skinless pork belly → pork shoulder; homemade chicken stock → low-sodium

Notes: You can find very thinly sliced pork belly and shoulder at many Asian markets.
There are many types of rice noodles, any of which will work here. I prefer a Chinese rice vermicelli in this recipe, though many Northeast Chinese homes prefer chewier cellophane noodles.

Make-ahead and storage: The tofu can be kept in the freezer for up to 6 months, then defrosted as needed.
author: Lucas Sin
